title: DevOps in Plain English: From Commit to Controlled Delivery
summary: Understand how source control, pull requests, pipelines, artifacts and deployment environments form one traceable delivery system.
plain_language_explanation: DevOps delivery is a chain of evidence. Code changes enter version control, pull requests apply review and policy, pipelines build and test repeatably, artifacts carry immutable outputs, and environments add deployment controls. Production safety depends on keeping those stages traceable rather than bypassing them when delivery is urgent.
quick_check: Why is a green build not by itself enough evidence that a production deployment should proceed?

title: Azure Repos, Pull Requests and Branch Protection
summary: Design repository and branch controls that preserve review, traceability and build validation before merge.
objective: Explain how repository permissions, pull requests, reviewers, linked work, build validation and status checks create a controlled merge path.
body_outline: Protect high-value branches by requiring pull requests instead of normal direct pushes.
Use minimum reviewer, comment-resolution, linked-work-item and build-validation policies where they match the repository risk profile.
Restrict policy-bypass and force-push permissions because those permissions can defeat otherwise strong controls.
Automatically include specialist reviewers for security, infrastructure or compliance-sensitive paths when ownership requires it.
Treat branch policies as merge controls, not as a substitute for secure repository permissions, testing or secret hygiene.
Preserve traceability from requirement or work item through commit, pull request, build and release evidence.

title: CI/CD Pipelines, Artifacts, Environments and Deployment Controls
summary: Build delivery pipelines that separate build evidence from deployment authority and protect production resources.
objective: Connect pipeline stages, immutable artifacts, environments, service connections and checks into a production-safe release model.
body_outline: Build once and promote a known artifact rather than rebuilding independently in each environment.
Use pipeline stages to make build, test, package and deployment responsibilities explicit.
Protect environments and other pipeline resources with approvals and checks owned outside editable pipeline YAML where separation of duties is required.
Treat service connections, variable groups, secure files and agent pools as privileged resources with their own access boundaries.
Do not store secrets directly in source or ordinary pipeline variables; use approved secret-management mechanisms and least privilege.
Deployment success should include post-deployment health verification and rollback or roll-forward criteria, not only a successful task exit code.

title: Production DevOps Control Loop: Secure Supply Chain, Evidence and Recovery
summary: Connect repository governance, pipeline security, artifact integrity, observability and recovery into one operating model.
architecture_notes: A production delivery system should preserve provenance from commit through reviewed pull request, validated pipeline, immutable artifact, approved environment and observed runtime. Controls should be layered: repository permissions, branch policies, pipeline permissions, resource checks, secret management, artifact integrity and runtime monitoring. Emergency paths need explicit ownership and post-event review rather than silent bypass.
failure_modes: direct push or policy bypass defeats required review and build validation
pipeline consumes a mutable dependency or rebuilds different artifacts for each environment
service connection has subscription-wide privilege when workload scope would be sufficient
secret appears in source, logs, artifacts or ordinary variables
approval exists in YAML and can be modified by the same change it is meant to govern
deployment task succeeds but application health or Azure Monitor signals degrade
rollback is attempted without proving database, schema or external dependency compatibility
enterprise_design_notes: Use immutable promotion, least-privilege identities, protected environments, independent checks, artifact provenance, observable deployments and rehearsed recovery. Treat pipeline configuration as production code and protect it accordingly.

title: Read-Only Azure DevOps Delivery Evidence Pack
summary: Audit repository, branch, pipeline and environment metadata without changing policies, secrets, service connections or deployments.
objective: Produce a timestamped delivery-control inventory before any repository, pipeline or deployment-control change is proposed.
steps: Confirm the approved Azure DevOps organization, project and repository before collecting evidence.
Record default branch and inspect branch-policy configuration without changing permissions or bypass settings.
Inventory pipeline definitions, recent runs and stage structure without queuing or rerunning a pipeline.
Record referenced environments, service connections, variable groups and secure resources without reading secret values or modifying permissions.
Trace one representative change from commit or pull request through build artifact and deployment evidence where available.
Document missing reviews, validation, approvals, ownership or observability as findings rather than correcting them during discovery.
expected_result: A read-only DevOps evidence pack covering repository controls, pipelines and delivery-resource metadata with no mutation, secret disclosure or deployment.
rollback: Not required; prescribed commands are inventory operations.

title: CI/CD Failure and Unsafe Deployment Decision Tree
summary: Separate source, policy, agent, dependency, artifact, authorization and runtime failures before bypassing delivery controls.
diagnostic_order: Identify whether the failure is repository/branch policy, pipeline syntax, agent capability, dependency retrieval, test, artifact publication, approval/check, service-connection authorization or runtime health.
Preserve the exact run, commit, stage, job and task evidence before rerunning anything.
Confirm the artifact and source revision being evaluated rather than assuming the latest branch state matches the failed run.
Check resource authorization and approval/check results before increasing pipeline or service-connection privilege.
For deployment failures, compare target environment state and application health with pre-deployment evidence before retrying.
Escalate when resolution requires bypassing branch policies, exposing secrets, broadening privileged identities, modifying protected environments or forcing a production deployment.
escalation_boundary: Do not bypass required reviews/checks, force-push protected history, reveal secret values, grant broad service-connection access, alter production approvals or trigger a production deployment from this troubleshooting workflow without explicit change authority.

title: DevOps / AZ-400 Foundations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering repository governance, CI/CD, artifacts, approvals, security and deployment evidence.

assessment_items.question: Why protect a main branch with both permissions and branch policies?
assessment_items.answer: Policies require review and validation, while permissions restrict who can push, administer or bypass those controls. Either layer alone can leave avoidable gaps.

assessment_items.question: Why build an artifact once and promote it?
assessment_items.answer: It preserves provenance and reduces the risk that different environments receive different outputs from the same source revision.

assessment_items.question: Why are environment checks stronger when controlled by the resource owner rather than only written in pipeline YAML?
assessment_items.answer: They create separation of duties because a pipeline author cannot simply edit the same YAML change to remove the independent gate.

assessment_items.question: What evidence should be checked after a deployment task reports success?
assessment_items.answer: Target-state verification, application health, telemetry and alerts, plus any required business or synthetic checks before declaring the release healthy.

title: Senior DevOps Interview: Secure Delivery and Release Governance
summary: Senior scenarios testing pull-request controls, pipeline architecture, privileged resources, observability and recovery.

questions.question: A production hotfix is urgent and branch policy is blocking the merge. What do you do?
answer_points: use a documented emergency path only if authorized
limit any bypass to named owners
do not force-push or silently remove policy

questions.question: A pipeline works in test but production deployment is denied. How do you isolate the issue?
answer_points: separate pipeline logic from target RBAC or Policy
avoid granting broad Owner access as a diagnostic shortcut

questions.question: How do you design a secure service connection?
answer_points: no secret exposure in logs or source
